newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash prods firm with NYMEX, most diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash prods firm with NYMEX, most diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices followed NYMEX to gains of about 0.75 cent a gallon at both centers, amid hightened concern over developments in Iraq, industry sources said.
Buyers on the futures market were sparked by report of troop movements in the nation, sending the October crude oil contract to levels just below its lifetime highs.
But cash market dealings were less than enthusiastic at both centers, with differntials slightly weaker than in previous sessions.
Concerns about heating oil stocks have not yet driven cash traders to rush the cash market for barrels. And Gasoline players were looking to coming changes in seasonal specifications.
A squeeze on premium barrels in New York pushed up offers for lower RVP premium gasoline in New York and in the U.S. Gulf. Diffs for RFG barrels were stable to lower.
Talk of a rush to send Low sulfur diesel to Europe continued, but differentials eased somewhat from lofty levels seen on the U.S. Gulf Coast in previous days.
Traders were eager to see API's inventory data, which is expected to show a seasonal change in stock levels.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
